# Slack Web API Reference

Companion to SKILL.md. Read this when choosing a method, setting up app scopes, checking exact parameter names, or debugging errors.

## Table of Contents

- [Authentication and Scopes](#authentication-and-scopes)
- [Message Formatting (mrkdwn)](#message-formatting-mrkdwn)
- [Method Catalog](#method-catalog)
  - [Messaging](#messaging)
  - [Channels and Conversations](#channels-and-conversations)
  - [Users and Team](#users-and-team)
  - [Files](#files)
  - [Reactions](#reactions)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Errors and Rate Limits](#errors-and-rate-limits)
- [Limitations](#limitations)

## Authentication and Scopes

- All requests: `POST https://slack.com/api/<METHOD>` with header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and a JSON body. The bundled helper (`scripts/slack_api.py`) does this for you.
- Token types: **bot token** (`xoxb-...`) acts as the app; **user token** (`xoxp-...`) acts as a user. Some methods require one specific type.
- The app must be installed in the workspace with the needed scopes. Common bot-token scopes by task:

| Task | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| Send/update/delete messages, ephemeral messages | `chat:write` |
| List channels, read channel history | `channels:read`, `channels:history` |
| Private channels (groups) | `groups:read`, `groups:history` (app must be a member) |
| DMs with users | `im:read`, `im:history` (to read); sending DMs needs `chat:write` + an open IM |
| Look up users by email / list users | `users:read`, `users:read.email` |
| Upload files | `files:write` |
| Read file metadata | `files:read` |
| Add/remove reactions | `reactions:write` |
| Workspace info | `team:read` |

- A `missing_scope` / `not_allowed_token_type` error usually means the app manifest is missing a scope or the wrong token type is being used. Update scopes and reinstall the app.
- Never put the token inside the JSON body; always use the `Authorization` header. Never print or commit tokens.

## Message Formatting (mrkdwn)

Slack text supports a lightweight markup. Examples:

| You write | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `*bold*` | bold |
| `_italic_` | italic |
| `` `code` `` | inline code |
| `> quote line` | blockquote |
| `<https://example.com|Example>` | hyperlink with label |
| `<@U0123ABC>` | mention a user (by ID) |
| `<#C0123ABC|general>` | link a channel (by ID) |
| `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>` | special mentions (use sparingly) |
| `:tada:` | emoji |

- Escape literal `&`, `<`, `>` in untrusted/user-supplied text as `&`, `<`, `>`.
- Newlines in JSON strings (`\n`) render as line breaks.
- Plain `text` is limited to 40,000 characters.
- Rich layouts use a `blocks` array (Block Kit). If `blocks` is present, keep `text` as a short plain-text fallback for notifications. Never use legacy `attachments` for new code.

## Method Catalog

All methods return `{"ok": true, ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`. Required params are marked with `*`.

### Messaging

- **chat.postMessage** — send a message or thread reply. Params: `channel`*, `text` (or `blocks`), `thread_ts` (parent message ts to reply in-thread), `link_names` (1 to render user/channel names), `unfurl_links`. Scope: `chat:write`.
- **chat.postEphemeral** — message visible only to one user. Params: `channel`*, `user`*, `text`. Scope: `chat:write`.
- **chat.update** — edit a message the app sent. Params: `channel`*, `ts`*, `text`. Scope: `chat:write`.
- **chat.delete** — delete a message the app sent. Params: `channel`*, `ts`*. Scope: `chat:write`.
- **chat.scheduleMessage** — schedule a message. Params: `channel`*, `text`, `post_at`* (unix time). Scope: `chat:write`.
- **chat.getPermalink** — public URL of a message. Params: `channel`*, `message_ts`*. Scope: none.

### Channels and Conversations

- **conversations.list** — list channels the app can see. Params: `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`), `limit` (default 100), `cursor`. Use it to map channel names to IDs. Scopes: `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`.
- **conversations.info** — metadata for one conversation. Params: `channel`*. Scope: matching read scope.
- **conversations.history** — recent messages in a channel. Params: `channel`*, `limit` (default 100), `oldest`/`latest` (ts), `inclusive`. Paginate with `cursor`; check `has_more`. Scopes: `channels:history` / `groups:history` / `im:history`.
- **conversations.replies** — all messages in a thread. Params: `channel`*, `ts`* (thread root). Scope: matching history scope.
- **conversations.members** — members of a channel. Params: `channel`*, `cursor`. Scope: matching read scope.
- **conversations.open** — open a DM. Params: `users`* (comma-separated IDs; for a bot→user DM pass one user). Returns the IM `channel.id`, which you then use with `chat.postMessage`.
- **conversations.join** — app joins a public (or private, if invited) channel. Params: `channel`*. Fixes `not_in_channel`.
- **conversations.leave** — app leaves a channel. Params: `channel`*.
- **conversations.create / rename / archive / unarchive / setTopic / setPurpose / invite** — channel administration. Scopes: `channels:manage`, `groups:write`, `channels:write.invites` (invite). Many are restricted by workspace policy.

### Users and Team

- **users.lookupByEmail** — find a user by email. Params: `email`*. Scope: `users:read.email`.
- **users.info** — profile for one user. Params: `user`*. Scope: `users:read`.
- **users.list** — all users (paginated, `limit`/`cursor`; profiles are limited unless `include_locale` etc.). Scope: `users:read`.
- **users.conversations** — conversations a user is in. Scope: matching read scope.
- **team.info** — workspace name/domain. Scope: `team:read`.
- **auth.test** — verify the token and see whose it is. No scope needed. Always a safe first call.

### Files

- **files.getUploadURLExternal** — start a two-step upload (the supported path; `files.upload` is deprecated). Params: `filename`*, `length`* (bytes), `alt_text`. Returns `upload_url` and `file_id`. Supports files up to 1 GB.
- (upload step) — send the file bytes to the returned `upload_url` with `POST` (multipart form field `file`, or raw body). This is a plain HTTP call, not a Web API method: `curl -F file=@report.csv "<upload_url>"`.
- **files.completeUploadExternal** — finish the upload and optionally share it. Params: `files`* (`[{"id":"F...","title":"..."}]`), `channel_id` (share into a channel), `thread_ts`. Scope: `files:write`.
- **files.info** — metadata for an uploaded file. Params: `file`*. Scope: `files:read`.
- Do not use **files.upload** (legacy, deprecated by Slack).

### Reactions

- **reactions.add** — add an emoji reaction. Params: `channel`*, `name`* (emoji without colons, e.g. `thumbsup`), `timestamp`* (target message ts). Scope: `reactions:write`.
- **reactions.remove** — Params: `channel`*, `name`*, `timestamp`*. Scope: `reactions:write`.
- **reactions.get** — reactions on a message. Params: `channel`*, `timestamp`*. Scope: `reactions:read`.

## Pagination

List/history methods paginate with cursors:

1. Call the method with `cursor` omitted (or `""`).
2. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the response.
3. If it is non-empty, repeat the call with `cursor: "<next_cursor>"` and merge the results.
4. Stop when `next_cursor` is empty (history also reports `has_more: false`).

Never assume one page is the full answer. Set a sane page cap (e.g. 10 pages) to avoid runaway loops.

## Errors and Rate Limits

- Normal failures return HTTP 200 with `ok: false` and an `error` name. The helper prints a fix hint for common ones: `invalid_auth`, `account_inactive`, `missing_scope`, `not_allowed_token_type`, `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel` (join with `conversations.join`), `is_archived`, `user_not_found`, `invalid_blocks`, `no_text`, `message_too_long` (40k cap), `restricted_action`, `internal_error` (retry).
- HTTP 429 = rate limited. Honor the `Retry-After` header before retrying. Default tiers allow roughly 1+ requests/second per method; stay conservative.
- HTTP 5xx = transient Slack failure; retry once after a short delay.
- `response_metadata.messages` (when present) carries extra human-readable detail about the failure.

## Limitations

- The app can only see and act on channels it is a member of (public channels can be joined via `conversations.join`; private channels need an invite).
- A bot cannot read or post to private channels/DMs unless it has been added to them.
- Workspace/enterprise policies can block DMs or file uploads (`restricted_action`).
- `search.messages` is deprecated (SearchKit migration); prefer `conversations.history`/`conversations.list` and client-side filtering.
- Files: use the two-step `files.getUploadURLExternal` + `files.completeUploadExternal` flow; one-step `files.upload` is deprecated.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Command-line client for the Slack Web API.

Usage:
  python3 slack_api.py <METHOD> ['{"param": "value", ...}'] [--token TOKEN] [--max-chars N]

Examples:
  python3 slack_api.py auth.test
  python3 slack_api.py chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123ABC","text":"Hello *world*"}'
  python3 slack_api.py conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel,private_channel","limit":200}'

The token comes from --token or the SLACK_TOKEN environment variable (preferred).
The token is always sent in the Authorization header, never in the body.

Exit codes:
  0  Slack returned ok: true
  1  Slack returned ok: false, or an HTTP/network error occurred
  2  Local usage error (missing token, malformed JSON, ...)
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

API_BASE = "https://slack.com/api/"
DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 4000

# Common Slack error names mapped to the most likely fix.
ERROR_HINTS = {
    "invalid_auth": "the token is invalid or was revoked - check SLACK_TOKEN",
    "account_inactive": "the app/user behind the token was deactivated",
    "missing_scope": "the app is missing a required scope - see references/api.md and reinstall the app",
    "not_allowed_token_type": "this method needs a different token type (bot vs user) - see references/api.md",
    "channel_not_found": "no such channel, or the app cannot see it - list channels with conversations.list",
    "not_in_channel": "the app is not a member of that channel - join it with conversations.join",
    "is_archived": "the channel is archived - pick another channel or unarchive it",
    "user_not_found": "no such user - resolve the ID with users.list or users.lookupByEmail",
    "invalid_blocks": "blocks JSON is malformed - validate against the Block Kit reference",
    "no_text": "provide a text field, or blocks containing text",
    "message_too_long": "text exceeds the 40,000 character limit",
    "restricted_action": "workspace or enterprise policy blocked this action",
    "internal_error": "transient Slack-side failure - retry once after a short delay",
}


def _parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Call the Slack Web API.")
    parser.add_argument("method", help="Slack API method, e.g. chat.postMessage")
    parser.add_argument(
        "params",
        nargs="?",
        default="{}",
        help='JSON object of parameters, e.g. \'{"channel":"C123","text":"hi"}\'',
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--token", default=None, help="Slack token (defaults to $SLACK_TOKEN)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-chars",
        type=int,
        default=DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS,
        help="max response characters printed (0 = unlimited)",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def _hint(error):
    hint = ERROR_HINTS.get(error)
    return f" - {hint}" if hint else ""


def main():
    args = _parse_args()
    token = args.token or os.environ.get("SLACK_TOKEN", "")
    if not token:
        print(
            "error: no token: set the SLACK_TOKEN environment variable or pass --token",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)

    try:
        params = json.loads(args.params)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        print(f"error: params is not valid JSON: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    if not isinstance(params, dict):
        print("error: params must be a JSON object", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    if "token" in params:
        print(
            "warning: removing 'token' from the body; the token is sent in the Authorization header",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        params.pop("token")

    payload = json.dumps(params).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        API_BASE + args.method,
        data=payload,
        method="POST",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
        },
    )

    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
            raw = response.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        if exc.code == 429:
            retry_after = exc.headers.get("Retry-After", "?")
            print(
                f"slack error: rate_limited (HTTP 429) - retry after {retry_after}s",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        elif exc.code >= 500:
            print(
                f"slack error: transient HTTP {exc.code} - retry once after a short delay",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        else:
            body = exc.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
            try:
                error = json.loads(body).get("error", "http_error")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                error = f"http_{exc.code}"
            print(f"slack error: {error} (HTTP {exc.code}){_hint(error)}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        print(f"error: could not reach Slack: {exc.reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        print("error: Slack returned a non-JSON response; aborting", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    if data.get("ok") is not True:
        error = data.get("error", "unknown_error")
        message = f"slack error: {error}{_hint(error)}"
        details = (data.get("response_metadata") or {}).get("messages")
        if details:
            message += f" | details: {'; '.join(details)}"
        print(message, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    text = json.dumps(data, indent=2)
    limit = args.max_chars
    if limit and limit > 0 and len(text) > limit:
        print(text[:limit])
        print(
            f"... (response truncated to {limit} chars; rerun with --max-chars 0 for the full body)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    else:
        print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

name: slack-api
description: Interact with Slack workspaces through the Slack Web API. Use when the user asks to post or schedule messages, reply in threads, send DMs or channel notifications, list or search channels, read conversation history, look up users, upload files, or add emoji reactions in Slack using a bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Send and retrieve Slack data via the Web API. Make every call with the bundled helper script (`scripts/slack_api.py`), which handles authentication, JSON encoding, error checking, and output formatting. Read `references/api.md` for the full method catalog, required scopes, formatting rules, and error reference — consult it when choosing a method or debugging.

## Setup

- Provide a token for an app installed in the target workspace: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (preferred) or pass `--token`. Never print, log, or commit tokens. If no token is set, ask the user for one — never invent one.
- Helper usage: `python3 scripts/slack_api.py <METHOD> '<json params>' [--token TOKEN] [--max-chars N]`

Sanity-check the token first:

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py auth.test
```

The script prints the JSON response to stdout, exits `0` only when Slack reports `ok: true`, and prints a fix hint on errors (e.g. `not_in_channel`, `missing_scope`).

## Core Tasks

### Post a message to a channel

Use `chat.postMessage` with the channel ID (prefer IDs — resolve names first, see below) and `text` (mrkdwn allowed). Use a `blocks` array for rich messages and keep `text` as a short plain-text fallback:

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123ABC","text":"*Standup* moved to 10:30 <https://cal.example.com|calendar>","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Standup* moved to 10:30 <https://cal.example.com|calendar>"}}]}'
```

### Reply in a thread

Same as posting, plus the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`:

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C0123ABC","thread_ts":"1712345678.123456","text":"+1"}'
```

### Send a DM to a user

1. Resolve the user ID: `users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'`
2. Open the DM: `conversations.open '{"users":"U0123ABC"}'` — returns the IM `channel.id`
3. Post to that channel with `chat.postMessage`.

### Resolve channel and user names to IDs

Conversation and user IDs are the reliable keys; names are ambiguous. Map names with:

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel,private_channel","limit":200}'
```

The app only sees channels it belongs to (join public ones with `conversations.join`; private ones require an invite). Resolve users with `users.list` or `users.lookupByEmail`. Then pass IDs, not names.

### Read conversation history

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py conversations.history '{"channel":"C0123ABC","limit":100}'
```

Repeat with `cursor` while `response_metadata.next_cursor` is non-empty; threads via `conversations.replies` with the root `ts`. Do not assume one page is everything.

### Upload a file to a channel

`files.upload` is deprecated — always use the two-step flow:

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal '{"filename":"report.csv","length":1234,"alt_text":"Q3 numbers"}'` → returns `upload_url` + `file_id`
2. Send the file bytes to that `upload_url` (plain HTTP, not a Web API call): `curl -F file=@report.csv "<upload_url>"`
3. `files.completeUploadExternal '{"files":[{"id":"F0123ABC","title":"report.csv"}],"channel_id":"C0123ABC"}'`

### Add a reaction

```
python3 scripts/slack_api.py reactions.add '{"channel":"C0123ABC","name":"thumbsup","timestamp":"1712345678.123456"}'
```

The `name` is the emoji without colons; `timestamp` is the target message's `ts`.

### Update or delete a message

`chat.update` / `chat.delete` with `channel` + `ts` of a message the app posted (workspace policy may restrict this).

## Rules of Thumb

- **Check the envelope**: trust data only after `ok: true`; on failure read the `error` name and the script's hint.
- **IDs over names**: resolve via `conversations.list` / `users.*` before calling message methods.
- **Formatting**: mrkdwn — `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `> quote`, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U0123ABC>`, `<#C0123ABC|general>`, `:wave:`. Escape literal `&`, `<`, `>` in user-supplied text (`&`, `<`, `>`). Text max 40,000 chars.
- **Pagination**: follow `response_metadata.next_cursor` until empty; cap at ~10 pages.
- **Rate limits**: be conservative (~1 req/s per method); on HTTP 429 honor `Retry-After`.
- **Discretion**: confirm before broadcasting to wide-audience channels; prefer threads for follow-ups and keep messages concise and useful.
- See `references/api.md` for scopes per task (e.g. `chat:write`, `channels:history`, `files:write`) and the full error catalog.

## Resources

- `scripts/slack_api.py` — the API helper used for all calls. Read it only if it needs patching or environment-specific adjustment.
- `references/api.md` — endpoint catalog with parameters and scopes, mrkdwn guide, pagination, errors, and limitations. Read it when choosing a method, setting up scopes, or debugging.
